features: FileHandle.readableWebStream now creates a byte stream backed by FileHandle.read and its real reference-counted native I/O instead of delegating directly to Bun.file(fd).stream. Default and BYOB readers consume file bytes, including empty EOF.

autoClose is validated and honored on EOF and cancellation. The stream retains/relinquishes its handle reference once, removes its close listener at completion, and awaits a pending/native close when required. The default keeps descriptor ownership with the caller.

Closed/closing/locked handle and options validation are implemented. Non-bytes type options emit ExperimentalWarning while a byte stream is still created. Native controls cover default/BYOB reads, empty files, lazy cancellation, retained ownership, autoClose and repeated stream creation.

The unmodified filesystem/FileHandle selections and existing native stream/context/directory/performance groups pass. Rebase integrates a benchmark-only main update; the committed runtime source bytes exactly match the tested hashes.
limitations: Concurrent close during a native read, stale descriptor misuse, transfer/deserialization, every stream error/close failure and FileHandle.getAsyncId remain unverified or incomplete. Those excluded lifecycle fixtures were not run. General native producer/context integration remains #877.

Thirty-five original invocations yield 168 case passes plus twenty process checks, zero failures/skips/filters and two upstream async-context TODOs. TODOs receive no passing credit. Full Bun-suite parity is not established.

The initial Home autoClose failure, first/refined builds, reference controls, terminal cache cleanup, unchanged pinned hashes and all positive/negative report outcomes remain retained. Native ABI code was unchanged; fourteen targeted controls pass and broader ABI checks were not rerun.
Pickier retains five preexisting prefer-const errors and one quote warning, reproduced on the committed baseline. The new native controls add no lint findings.

Corpus #876, context #871/#856, directory queued/platform proof #878, performance #869/#873/#874/#872 and HTTPS #875/#532 remain open under #66. Known excluded regressions and Release/ASAN/all-platform validation were not rerun.
